text:
The primary material of a candle is wax, which serves as the fuel source that melts and is drawn up the wick to sustain the flame.

The city at night is a canvas of light, each skyscraper a brushstroke of vibrant fluorescence against the deep indigo of the twilight sky, painting an urban masterpiece that wakes up as the rest of the world sleeps. In this nocturnal tableau, the buildings stand like silent sentinels, their glass facades reflecting the starlight as mirrors in a hall of echoes. The streets below flow like rivers of neon, carrying the lifeblood of the metropolis in a ceaseless, rhythmic pulse. Just as a candle’s wax slowly surrenders itself to the flame, the city consumes the day’s energy to ignite its own vibrant existence, burning bright against the encroaching dark.
